tasks.title: Lecture #50
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk on a history podcast.
tasks.transcript:
In the 19th century, cities in the United States became crowded. Many businesses and apartments were housed in tall buildings. Fires became a major concern. Most firetruck ladders only reached the fourth floor, which wasn't high enough.
Although laws were passed to require escape routes, many early ideas were impractical, like one idea was to attach a parachute to your head. The parachute idea, well, this wouldn't work too well, would it?
Other such ideas were met with resistance, too.
Enter Anna Connolly, who received patterns for fire escapes in the 19th century. Anna Connolly's initial fire escape design was a bridge so people could safely go up to the roof or upper floors of their own building, cross to the building next door, and go down the stairs there. This made good sense since most fires started on the lower floors of buildings.
After this design, Connolly created another that was a series of platforms attached to the side of a building with ladders connecting them. She specified they'd be made of iron, since iron is fireproof and resists pressure.
Well, this design worked, was practical, and was adopted across the country. Connolly's fire escapes saved lives.
These days, buildings in the US are built with interior stairwells that are fireproof for escape and are not visible from the outside. But you can still see Connolly's design on older buildings in cities.

questions.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?

options.A: A problem that was solved by a group of women inventors
options.B: A safety concern with nineteenth-century firetrucks
options.C: A way to prevent fires in tall buildings
options.D: An invention that improved safety in cities

questions.analysis: 答案：D 题目问的是：这次谈话的主要话题是什么？ 定 位 原 文 ： Enter Anna Connolly, who received patterns for fire escapes in the 19th century. ... Connolly's fire escapes saved lives. ... These days... you can still see Connolly's design on older buildings in cities. 选项分析： A. 一个由一群女性发明家解决的问题。谈话只提到了一位女性发明家 Anna Connolly，并非“一群”，因此 A 选项错误。 B. 十九世纪消防车的一个安全隐患。谈话提到消防车梯子不够高是背景问题，但重点不是消防车本身，因此 B 选项错误。 C. 一种预防高楼火灾的方法。谈话讨论的是火灾发生后的逃生方法，而非预防火灾，因此C 选项错误。 D. 一项提高了城市安全的发明。谈话围绕 Anna Connolly 设计的防火梯展开，说明了其工作原理、实用性以及拯救生命的作用，因此 D 选项正确。

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention a parachute?

options.A: To highlight a problem with some designs
options.B: To give an example of a modern solution
options.C: To give an example of a patented invention
options.D: To emphasize the variety of businesses in cities

questions.analysis: 答案：A 题目问的是：演讲者为什么提到降落伞？ 定位原文：Although laws were passed to require escape routes, many early ideas were impractical, like one idea was to attach a parachute to your head. The parachute idea, well, this wouldn't work too well, would it? 选项分析： A. 为了突出某些设计存在的问题。演讲者用降落伞作为早期不切实际想法的例子，说明这些设计不可行，因此 A 选项正确。 B. 为了给出一个现代解决方案的例子。降落伞是 19 世纪的不实用想法，并非现代解决方案，因此 B 选项错误。 C. 为了给出一个专利发明的例子。谈话没有提到降落伞是否获得专利，因此 C 选项错误。 D. 为了强调城市中商业的多样性。这与降落伞无关，因此 D 选项错误。

questions.stem: What does the speaker like about Anna Connelly's first design?

options.A: It was the least expensive option.
options.B: It took into account the origins of most fires.
options.C: It had all of the features required by law.
options.D: It allowed firefighters to reach higher floors.

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：演讲者喜欢 Anna Connelly 第一个设计的哪一点？ 定位原文：Anna Connolly's initial fire escape design was a bridge so people could safely go up to the roof or upper floors of their own building, cross to the building next door, and go down the stairs there. This made good sense since most fires started on the lower floors of buildings. 选项分析： A. 它是最便宜的选择。谈话中没有提到成本比较，因此 A 选项错误。 B. 它考虑到了大多数火灾的起源。演讲者明确说这个设计“很有道理”，因为大多数火灾从低层开始，人们可以通过桥到隔壁下楼，因此 B 选项正确。 C. 它拥有法律要求的所有特征。谈话没有提及法律的具体要求，因此 C 选项错误。 D. 它允许消防员到达更高的楼层。这个设计是为居民逃生用的，而非消防员，因此 D 选项错误。

questions.stem: What does the speaker indicate about fire escapes in newer buildings?

options.A: They were inspired by Connelly's second design.
options.B: They are constructed with iron supports.
options.C: They cannot be seen from the outside.
options.D: They do not work as well as Connelly's inventions.

questions.analysis: 答案：C 题目问的是：关于新建筑中的防火梯，演讲者指出了什么？ 定 位 原 文 ： These days, buildings in the US are built with interior stairwells that are fireproof for escape and are not visible from the outside. 选项分析： A. 它们受到 Connelly 第二个设计的启发。演讲者没有说明新旧设计之间的灵感关系，因此 A 选项错误。 B. 它们用铁支架建造。新建筑使用的是内部防火楼梯间，没有提到铁支架，因此 B 选项错误。 C. 它们从外面看不到。原文明确指出新建筑的防火楼梯间“从外面看不见”，因此 C 选项正确。 D. 它们不如 Connelly 的发明有效。演讲者没有对新旧设计的有效性进行比较，因此 D 选项错误。
